transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-17
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE); Priya (Redwood SE); Marcus (Redwood Legal Ops); Lena (Nimbus Procurement); Tomás (Nimbus GC); Evelyn (Nimbus Cloud Eng); Samir (Nimbus CISO)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Discussed MSA redlines and DPA exception requests from Nimbus legal; clarified SLAs and pricing committee timeline; identified security artifacts needed (SOC2, KMS details, audit logs); agreed on next steps to send redlines and schedule a technical benchmark.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA exceptions, SLA targets, pricing approval flow, security attachments, dedicated vs hosted deployment, data residency, procurement committee timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we set aside about 45, 50 minutes, I know you had a packed agenda. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Lena (Nimbus Procurement): Hey Jordan, Lena here, Tomás on in a minute, Evelyn and Samir are with me.
[00:09] Tomás (Nimbus GC): Tomás here, sorry for the slight delay.
[00:12] Jordan (Redwood AE): No problem. Priya and Marcus from my side. Marcus is Redwood legal ops, so he'll picked up the DPA/MSA questions.
[00:18] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all. We'll try not to nerd out too hard until we need to.
[00:22] Samir (Nimbus CISO): Samir here. We're particularly focused on encryption at rest and audit logging retention. Also curious about key management integrations.
[00:29] Marcus (Redwood Legal Ops): Morning — or afternoon — yes, Tomás, happy to walk through redlines. We saw the list you sent, a couple of DPA exceptions that look negotiable, others are tougher.

[00:42] Jordan (Redwood AE): Goal for today's call: align on what you need for procurement and legal to move to pricing committee, and to make sure the security checklist is complete so we can avoid last-minute stalls.

[01:05] Evelyn (Nimbus Cloud Eng): Quick context — we run a hybrid footprint: most workloads in GCP, some sensitive ML workloads that may need VPC peering or private deployment. We need to know if Redwood Private supports air-gapped or at least VPC-only control plane.
[01:24] Priya (Redwood SE): Short answer: Redwood Private supports VPC peering and a customer-controlled control plane; on-prem air-gapped is available as a special engagement. There's a packaging path for on-prem but it involves additional ops and a different commercial model.
[01:39] Evelyn (Nimbus Cloud Eng): Ok that helps. Also curious about KV cache behavior — we want to understand retention and what lives in memory vs. disk.
[01:50] Priya (Redwood SE): Right, the KV cache is in-memory by default; we can persist to an encrypted store on‑disk if you choose; terminology in our docs sometimes shows "K-V cash" in automatic transcripts, but it's the KV cache.

[02:10] Tomás (Nimbus GC): On the DPA — we flagged two areas: data subject access timelines and subprocessors. We have tighter timelines than your standard DPA and need more granular subprocessors list.
[02:24] Marcus (Redwood Legal Ops): Understood. For DSARs we typically propose a 30‑day window with cooperation clauses; if you need shorter, we can look at operational commitments and add carve-outs to the MSA. Subprocessors — we can provide a current list plus commit to notifying changes within 30 days. Is that acceptable?
[02:45] Tomás (Nimbus GC): We prefer 15 days on DSARs and a right to audit certain subprocessors. That's a bit aggressive.
[02:52] Jordan (Redwood AE): Maybe to trade, we could offer shorter DSAR timeline for services under Dedicated or Private where we have more control — gives you stronger guarantees for the sensitive workloads.
[03:05] Samir (Nimbus CISO): That makes sense. For the CISO lens: encryption, KMS, and having a verifiable key separation model is priority. Do you integrate with external KMS (Cloud KMS, HashiCorp Vault, customer HSM)?
[03:20] Marcus (Redwood Legal Ops): We have integrations with major cloud KMSes and can support bring-your-own-key in certain Private deployments. If BYOK is required contractually, we need to document the responsibilities (key rotation, compromise handling) in the addendum.

[03:36] Priya (Redwood SE): On SLAs: typical hosted customers see p99 generation latencies in the 100–300ms band for short prompts and with bursty traffic we suggest Dedicated to guarantee p99 under high concurrency. For quantized models we can do lower latency; we'll share a latency vs cost matrix.
[03:55] Evelyn (Nimbus Cloud Eng): The procurement committee will ask for concrete numbers. Can you provide an SLA draft with p99 numbers for both hosted and Dedicated, as well as outage credits?
[04:07] Jordan (Redwood AE): Yes — next step, Priya will draft an SLA proposal. It will include outage credits, minimum uptime, and p99 ranges per class of model and commit level.

[04:20] Lena (Nimbus Procurement): On pricing, we need to present a comparison to the incumbent. We expect a pricing tier tied to committed tokens and a pilot discount. What are typical commercial motions?
[04:32] Jordan (Redwood AE): We offer usage-based pricing for hosted; reserved capacity (Dedicated) has a monthly commit plus overage rates. For procurement, we often provide a pilot discount and then scale to a commit aligned with expected monthly tokens. We'll put together an example pricing schedule for your finance team.

[04:52] Tomás (Nimbus GC): A couple redline items on indemnity and liability caps — Nimbus prefers a higher cap for breaches tied to customer data.
[05:02] Marcus (Redwood Legal Ops): Liability caps are often negotiable within enterprise pricing. We can look at a carve-out for data breaches with a higher cap if there's a material commit. We'll surface how that affects pricing.

[05:15] Samir (Nimbus CISO): Also we need detailed audit logs: per-request metadata, who accessed what, and timestamps. Retention options 90/180/365 days. Can you produce those?
[05:27] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, we emit audit logs and can retain per-request metadata. Retention is configurable in Dedicated/Private; hosted has default retention with add-on longer retention. Marcus will include exact retention SLAs in security artifacts.

[05:43] Speaker 1 (transcript auto-label): Uh, quick Q — when you say "Private" does that mean the entire control plane is customer-run or is it hybrid?
[05:50] Marcus (Redwood Legal Ops): Good question — Private can be either a customer-managed control plane or a private instance managed by Redwood inside your VPC depending on the engagement. We'll clarify in the DPA how responsibility shifts.

[06:05] Lena (Nimbus Procurement): Timeline constraints: Our pricing committee meets later this month; to get on the agenda, we need final redlines and the security pack by 9/24. Can you meet that?
[06:15] Jordan (Redwood AE): We can aim for that. Marcus and Priya, can we commit?
[06:20] Marcus (Redwood Legal Ops): Yes, we'll prioritize the DPA redlines and the security artifacts. We'll note exceptions that need exec-level signoff.
[06:29] Priya (Redwood SE): I'll assemble the SLA draft and the Dedicated throughput expectations; also include a short benchmark plan — we can run a small throughput test with your dataset to validate cost/latency trade-offs.

[06:45] Tomás (Nimbus GC): A procedural question — what's your process for notifying subprocessors when they change? We need a clause that allows us to pause use or require remediation.
[06:55] Marcus (Redwood Legal Ops): We notify changes 30 days in advance and provide an opt-out right if a subprocessor materially affects data processing. We can add a remediation window and, for critical subprocessors, allow you to request an alternative. Need to align on which ones are critical.

[07:13] Samir (Nimbus CISO): On the BYOK model — if we control keys, do you ever see data exfiltration risks because Redwood needs access to logs? How do you separate access levels?
[07:25] Priya (Redwood SE): With BYOK and Private deployments, control plane access is minimized; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM and we can maintain a zero-knowledge posture for customer keys depending on deployment. There's a support model for emergency access that is logged and requires approvals.

[07:40] Evelyn (Nimbus Cloud Eng): Also want to flag residency: some datasets must stay in EMEA. Do you support region pinning for models and embeddings?
[07:49] Jordan (Redwood AE): We do region pinning for hosted customers when contractual. Dedicated/Dedicated Private gives you stronger guarantees. We'll include region residency language in the DPA addendum.

[08:05] Lena (Nimbus Procurement): Ok, practical asks for procurement packet: 1) redlined MSA/DPA, 2) security pack (SOC2, pen test summary, encryption/KMS notes), 3) SLA draft with outage credits and p99 numbers, 4) pricing schedule/pilot terms.
[08:23] Jordan (Redwood AE): Noted — we will deliver those items. Marcus, Priya you'll own the docs plus Jordan will coordinate the pricing.

[08:33] Marcus (Redwood Legal Ops): One more nuance — your earlier email requested an indemnity carve-out for AI output. We typically limit indemnity for model hallucinations; that is a tough ask for us to accept broadly. We can discuss narrow carve-outs for certain regulated outputs under a POC.
[08:48] Tomás (Nimbus GC): Understood. For regulated outputs we may want explicit accuracy thresholds and rollback clauses.
[08:55] Priya (Redwood SE): For that we recommend evals and acceptance tests as part of the POC — if the model meets your acceptance criteria, we can tie certain warranties to that. We'll prepare a short eval plan.

[09:12] Speaker 2 (auto-label): There's a question about pricing approvals: do we need a full procurement RFP or will a vendor packet suffice?
[09:18] Lena (Nimbus Procurement): We'll use the vendor packet for initial committee review; if committee chooses Redwood we will likely run a formal vendor risk assessment which may include a questionnaire.

[09:30] Jordan (Redwood AE): We'll supply the questionnaire answers — we have a standard vendor security questionnaire and a completed packet we can share.

[09:38] Samir (Nimbus CISO): One operational ask: during onboarding, can we get a 30‑day support SLA with a named technical contact? That helps our ops team.

[09:45] Jordan (Redwood AE): Yes, named technical contact is included in enterprise packages; for pilots we can assign a solutions engineer for the duration.

[09:52] Priya (Redwood SE): About benchmarks — we recommend a two-phase POC: 1) functional/eval to validate outputs and safety, 2) performance test to map throughput and cost when running on Dedicated. We'll scope both and include test scripts.

[10:10] Lena (Nimbus Procurement): If we fast-track the pilot and the docs are good, we could escalate to the pricing committee and maybe get a tentative approval pending final legal sign-off.

[10:18] Jordan (Redwood AE): Great. Final recap before we end — Marcus will send redlined MSA/DPA and call out any exec-level exceptions; Priya will send the SLA draft + benchmark plan; Marcus will also attach SOC2 and KMS notes; Jordan will provide a pricing schedule and pilot commercial terms.

[10:38] Tomás (Nimbus GC): One ask: please mark any clauses that are absolute non-starters versus negotiable. That will speed review.
[10:45] Marcus (Redwood Legal Ops): Will do — we'll color-code items in a redline.

[10:52] Jordan (Redwood AE): Thanks everyone — we'll target the 9/19 and 9/20 deliverables, and aim to be on your 9/24 procurement packet.
[10:58] Lena (Nimbus Procurement): Thanks. We'll follow up with the procurement form and invite the right stakeholders to the pricing committee.
[11:03] Samir (Nimbus CISO): Thanks all.
[11:05] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcript quality: multiple auto-labels and occasional transcription artifacts ("K-V cash" for KV cache, "V-P-C" for VPC). Natural speech hesitations and cross talk present.
